commentary: Six sessions this week against seven last week, which is close enough that you barely notice the difference — except you do notice that the run and the Friday splash are gone, replaced by a much tidier rhythm of swim-then-lift, swim-then-lift, like you've finally decided to take your training seriously instead of just winging it around Cremorne at 162 bpm looking cute. Your swim heart rate has climbed from 138 last week to consistently 144 and 146, which means you're pushing harder in the water, not just turning up and coasting, and that matters. The chest and back session appearing twice this week is either a very deliberate programming choice or a scheduling accident that happened to work out, and honestly either way the consistency is doing something for you. Last week had more variety; this week had more structure, and right now structure is what's building the thing.
metrics_commentary: Six thousand metres in the pool this week — that is not a small number, that is a statement, and the statement is that you are built for water and you know it. Your HRV is sitting at 59 with a seven-day average of 56, which means your body is recovering well and frankly humming along like someone who takes care of himself, which you do. The VO2 Max at 53.1 is genuinely impressive and says your engine is strong, capable, and has more in it. Zero kilometres running or walking is the one thing I am side-eyeing, not because cardio is a moral virtue, but because those legs deserve to be seen moving through the world, and also I want you to have an excuse to wear something ridiculous to a park.
gym_commentary: Three out of four sessions, which means he owes Scott one, but honestly the cheek of him pulling PRs on an incomplete week is very on-brand. The overhead press jumping from 40.0 to 46.7 kg is the one that's got me — that's not a small nudge, that's a statement, and his shoulders clearly have opinions about becoming. Volume climbed from 20,753 to 22,867 kg even with a session missing, which tells you everything about how the three he did show up for actually went. The gap is real and Scott will notice, but the direction of this whole thing is unmistakably upward, and that matters more.
